To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rat liver CTP:phoshoethanolamine cyditylyltransferase, a key enzyme in the synthesis of phosphatidylethanoline (PE), was cloned, and that its expression was regulated during liver development.
the rat CTP:PE cytidyly transferase gene has been isolated, and that the amount of enzyme and its mRNA are regulated during rat liver development.

(1) the cDNA of rat CTP: phosphoethanolamine-cytidylyltransferase encodes a protein with two catalytic domains and a large repetitive internal structure; (2) transfection of COS cells resulted in a 11-fold increase of ET activity; (3) the amount of ET activity and protein in fetal rat liver increases during development, suggesting the regulation at both pretranscriptional and posttranscriptional levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning of a cDNA clone encoding a cytidylyttransferase from rat liver, which is the first step in elucidating the structure-function relationship of the enzyme and its regulation.

the cloning of rat liver ET cDNA, the characterization of the deduced amino acid sequences, the regulation of the expression of the cDNA, and the determination of the activity and amount of ET protein during rat liver development.
the cloning and expression of CDP-ethanoloamine synthetase cDNA from the liver of the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rat CTP:PE cytidylyttransferase is a 404 amino acid protein that is encoded by a cDNA that is approx. 2.2 kb in length and is expressed in rat liver.

the cloned rat ET cDNA is a functional cDNA encoding an enzyme that is very similar in sequence to human and yeast ETs and that the cloned cDNA is a useful tool for the study of the structure-function relationships and the regulation of rat ET.

the cDNA of ET was cloned from rat, the deduced amino acid sequences was very similar to that from humans, and that the cloned cDNA expressed a protein that was immunologically identical to the native ET.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rat ET is an integral membrane protein, which contains two active sites, and the expression of ET is regulated by both transcriptional and post-transcriptional mechanisms.
the cloned rat ET cDNA encodes an ET protein with a unique structural feature.
the cloned rat liver ET cDNA encodes the protein with the expected molecular mass and that it is a functional enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cloning and expression of ET cDNA from rat and human liver will provide a useful tool for studying ET structure, function, and regulation.
the ET cDNA clone can be used as a tool for studying the regulation of ET in vivo and for investigating the structure-function relationship in ET.
ET activity in rat liver is regulated at both the pretranslational level, through the transcription of the ET gene, and post-translationally, through the activation of the enzyme.
